name: Ritterin des Schwarzen Grals
mini: Trench-Crusade-Figur (eine Frau) aus der Black-Grail-Warband von Chris (17.10.): türkise Schuppenrüstung, rot-kupferne Schulterplatten, runder Helm mit nach vorn ragendem Stachel, blaues zerfetztes Cape, nur eine Waffe: blutverschmierte Speer-Hellebarde mit Gabelklinge. Rüstung voller Dreck und Rost, Hände blutig.

karte.name: Ritterin des Schwarzen Grals
karte.weapons: Gralsspeer | Nahkampf | A3 | DS(1), Stoß, Reißend
karte.look: a female plague knight in rusted, filthy teal scaled armour with a rust-red breastplate and pauldrons, a rounded rust-red helmet with a long forward-jutting black spike, tattered blue cloak, blood-smeared hands and a blood-coated forked polearm

prompt:
Create one image in portrait format 4:5 (if 4:5 is not available, use 2:3).

Style: a dramatic still frame from a big-budget live-action dark fantasy war film, the kind of shot that ends up on the poster. Photorealistic and cinematic: anamorphic lens, shallow depth of field, strong directional light with deep shadows, volumetric haze, fine film grain, a muted, slightly desaturated colour grade.

This is a real scene, not a model: the knight is a full-size living woman, played by a tall actress in a heavy practical costume with real weight, real corroded matte metal with no plastic sheen, wet mud and torn fabric, and a natural human stance with her weight on one leg and her body slightly turned. Never a miniature, figurine, action figure, toy or painted model.

Reference: the attached photo shows my hand-painted tabletop miniature. Recreate this exact character as a real woman, clearly female in build and armour: same pose, same armour, same helmet, same weapon, same colours. Change only the materials (real metal, cloth and leather instead of plastic and paint) and the proportions of a real human body. Do not invent a different helmet or armour. Do not show the base, the table or the room from the photo.

Subject, exactly as on the miniature: a female knight of the Black Grail, a plague knight from a war-torn trench world.
- Helmet: a rounded rust-red dome helmet with a dark face grille, and one long black serrated spike that juts forward from the front of the helmet like a beak. Not a crest on top, not a Greek or Spartan helmet.
- Armour: a high collar of teal-green scales, a rust-red breastplate clearly shaped for a woman's chest (two sculpted breast cups, as on the miniature), a narrower waist and hips, rust-red pauldrons, teal-green scaled sleeves, tassets and greaves over a black undersuit. Everything worn, rusted and dirty, with thick wet mud caked on her boots and lower legs.
- Her hands are smeared with blood up to the wrists, and blood is splattered across her armour.
- Cloak: a tattered, moth-eaten deep blue cloak hanging from her back.
- Weapon: only one, a long black polearm (somewhere between a spear and a halberd) with a forked rust-red blade, the blade and the upper shaft coated in blood. She holds it diagonally across her body in both hands with the blade raised high to one side. No other weapons: no sickles, no hook blades, no swords, no blades on her arms.

The moment: dusk in no man's land. She has just stopped in the smoke between shell craters, spear raised for the next thrust, cloak whipping in the wind, fine rain and ash in the air, her helmeted head turned towards the camera as if she has spotted her next victim. Fresh blood runs down the blade of her polearm.

Camera and light: low camera close to the ground, the knight towering over the viewer. Cold grey-blue ambient light, a hard warm rim light from behind outlining her silhouette and the edge of the cloak, her face hidden behind the grille.

Glowing accent: exactly one, a distant red signal flare far behind her, out of focus, whose red light catches the wet blood on the blade of her polearm. Nothing else in the image glows.

Background: dark and out of focus: churned mud, splintered wooden stakes, coils of rusted barbed wire, drifting smoke. No buildings, towers, moons, ships, floating objects or second figures.

Composition: portrait 4:5. The knight centred and filling most of the frame from head to knees or feet, the helmet in the upper third, the raised blade fully inside the frame. Keep a little dark, calm space above her head and near the top right corner, because the card's points badge sits there.

Not wanted: landscape format, a male knight, a flat male breastplate or masculine build, a different helmet than on the miniature, sickles or any second weapon, clean armour, miniature, figurine, action figure, toy, tabletop diorama, macro or tilt-shift photography, plastic or painted-model look, a static figure simply standing in a landscape. Also no digital painting, illustration, concept art, trading-card art, visible brush strokes, over-sharpened detail, oversaturated colours, fire or light effects all over the frame. No text, lettering, numbers, logos, card frame, border or user interface.
